title: Ridgeline Pro Credit Credit Risk Schedule — Hold, Charge-Off and Over-Limit Thresholds
content:
Commercial Credit stops charging on a Ridgeline Pro Credit account, and later charges it off, at the days-past-due figures of its tier. Days past due are those of the oldest unpaid invoice or minimum.

| Tier | Placed on hold at (days past due) | Charged off at (days past due) | Hold released only when every past-due amount is paid | Over-limit tolerance (percent above the credit line) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ridgeline Pro Revolving Charge | 60 | 180 | Yes | 0 |
| Ridgeline Pro Revolving Charge Plus | 60 | 180 | Yes | 0 |
| Ridgeline Commercial Account Net 30 | 30 | 180 | Yes | 10 |
| Ridgeline Commercial Account Net 30 Select | 45 | 180 | Yes | 10 |
| Ridgeline Commercial Account Net 45 | 45 | 180 | Yes | 10 |
| Ridgeline Commercial Account Net 60 Enterprise | 60 | 180 | Yes | 15 |

## How the figures read

- "Placed on hold at" is met at the figure itself: a Net 30 statement showing exactly 30 days past due reaches the hold figure; one showing 29 does not.
- On every tier an on-hold account is released only when every past-due amount is paid; there is no partial release.
- The over-limit tolerance is the percentage above the credit line the balance may reach before the account goes on hold. With 0 on the revolving tiers, any balance above the line is beyond tolerance.

Hypothetical illustration: a Commercial Account Net 60 Enterprise with a credit line of 400000.00 tolerates a balance up to 15 percent above the line, that is up to 460000.00; a balance of 460000.01 is beyond tolerance.
